newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BODY TO PROBE S.AFRICAN WINE INDUSTRY RESTRUCTURE.
newsitem.headline: BODY TO PROBE S.AFRICAN WINE INDUSTRY RESTRUCTURE.

text.p: South African Land Agriculture Minister, Derek Hanekom, would appoint a committee to investigate the regulation of the country's wine and distilling industries, the national agriculture department said.
The department said on Wednesday the move follows a meeting last Friday between representatives of wine co-operative KWV, the minister and national department.

In December Hanekom blocked plans by KWV to change from a statutory co-operative to a private company. He said at the time the bid would be delayed until he was satisfied that it was in the best interests of the wine industry.

Wednesday's statement said Hanekom had further indicated his intention to investigate the implications on competition in the wine and distilling industry that might follow KWV's proposed restructuring.
An audit of the assets held or controlled by KWV would also be held.

In December Hanekom said he was concerned that monies and resources which were accumulated for the purposes of the KWV's regulatory function might be distributed amongst present KWV members as part of their scheme of arrangement.

The committee to probe the industry would be headed by Eckart Kassier, the recently appointed head of the National Agricultural Marketing Council, a body which advises government on farming policy, the statement said.
